newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian grain conditions good for 70 mln T output.
newsitem.headline: Russian grain conditions good for 70 mln T output.

text.p: Growing conditions for Russian grains this season continue to be favourable and agricultural analysts said they were looking for a 1997 net grain harvest of 70 to 75 million tonnes.
"Nothing has really changed - everything remains very favourable (for the crops)," said Viktor Trenin of the State Meteorological Service by telephone.
He said recent rains in the European part of Russia had helped crops and rising temperatures in other regions had also been favourable.
"There were low temperatures in some areas, but now the weather has improved," he said.
Trenin said the main threat to this year's crop, lack of moisture, was in Siberia and July would be a crucial time.
Grain analysts said favourable growing conditions so far this season should ensure a crop at least as big as last year's.
Russia's 1996 output was a mediocre 69.3 million tonnes, well up on 63.4 million recorded in 1995 but still the second worst crop on record since 1965.

"At the moment, our original forecast of 70 to 75 million tonnes this year still holds," said Andrei Sizov of SovEcon Ltd, a private agricultural consultancy in Moscow. "There are no problems with growing conditions."
Vladimir Totsky, deputy director of Russia's Grain Union, a private grouping of traders and producers, said farmers were concentrating efforts on boosting wheat output to meet domestic demand.
"Of course, everything still depends on the weather," he said. "But at the moment, our estimates for the wheat crop are rising and we are now looking at a wheat crop of over 36 million tonnes."

Russian produced 34.9 million tonnes of wheat and 15.9 million tonnes of barley last year. Analysts pegged this year's barley crop at 16-17 million tonnes if favourable conditions continued. --Mike Collett-White, Moscow Newsroom +7095 941 8520
